did.abstract: A booklet of black-and-white photographs of members of the Teale family that have been commercially reproduced onto thick paper and bound.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Source and date of acquisition for this collection are unknown. The collection was formally accessioned in 1974.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: This small collection is housed in a single folder. Though the booklet is disbound, the pages' original order is retained. The sequence of the items' object ID numbers matches this original order.

bioghist.head: Biographical note
bioghist.p: Charles E. Teale (b. 1843) was a Brooklyn clothier who served as city magistrate for the City of Brooklyn and later as city magistrate for New York City following consolidation. Teale was born in Nottingham, England on June 1, 1843. He immigrated to Brooklyn when he was six years old and lived in Brooklyn for the remainder of his life. He attended Public School 8 but left school when he was 12 years old to work as an errand boy in the Young Men's Christian Association (Y.M.C.A.). From ages 14 to 18 he worked in the carpentry trade, leaving that trade to then work as a salesman at Henry and John Paret's wholesale clothing house. In 1871, Teale partnered with F.T. Hoyt to start Hoyt & Teale, a retail clothing business. Three years later, he opened his own merchant tailor business, Teale & Co., located at 611 Fulton Street. Teale was appointed a member of the Board of Education by Brooklyn Mayor James Howell, a position to which he was reappointed numerous times. He was also a member of the board of directors of the Y.M.C.A., a member of the Oxford Club, and a member of the Hanson Place M.E. Church, among other activities.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: Collection rehoused and finding aid revised by Dee Bowers in September 2026. At that time, the booklet was disbound and removed from the pamphlet binder in which it had originally been housed, as the front cover and first page had detached due to the nature of the binder. Brittle and browned interleaving tissue paper was removed and discarded, along with the blank back cover of the booklet.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Charles E. Teale family photobook, dating from circa 1895, consists of black-and-white photographs of members of the Teale family that have been commercially reproduced onto thick paper and bound into a booklet. Inserted into the photobook is a mounted clipping of a biographical sketch of Charles E. Teale that was published in Brooklyn Life magazine on July 20, 1895. The first page of the photobook is inscribed in ink with "Wishing you a Merry Xmas." The photobook includes photographic prints of Charles E. Teale and his wife (unnamed), Charles B. Teale and his wife (unnamed), Edward L. Teale, Carrie Teale, Charles H. Rue, Florence Teale Rue, Charles Teale Rue and Florence Rue (children), and a family home near the Brooklyn neighborhood of Bensonhurst.
